verifications.claim: The April 2026 Windows update addresses 164 vulnerabilities.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R2: 'A total of 167 security issues have been addressed.' R4: 'this month's update addresses a whopping 164 vulnerabilities'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict on exact number: R2 states 167, R4 states 164 for the same April 2026 update.

verifications.claim: The April 2026 Windows update addresses 8 critical vulnerabilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Eight of the vulnerabilities patched have a critical severity rating.' R4: 'Eight of the security bugs are rated critical'
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly confirm 8 critical vulnerabilities in the April 2026 update.

verifications.claim: The April 2026 Windows update addresses 2 zero-day flaws.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Amongst this number are two zero-day vulnerabilities.' R4: 'two are deemed zero-day flaws.'
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly state 2 zero-days patched in April 2026 update.

verifications.claim: The April 2026 Windows update includes Secure Boot certificate updates.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Arriving this week with the April Patch Tuesday updates... new visual clue... latest Secure Boot updates... To get the new Secure Boot certificates, just make sure you've applied the latest Windows updates.' R6: 'Windows quality updates include additional... new Secure Boot certificates.'
verifications.reasoning: R4 explicitly ties new Secure Boot certificates to April Patch Tuesday; R6 describes inclusion in quality updates.

verifications.claim: Older Secure Boot certificates are expiring in June.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'replace older Secure Boot certificates before they expire in June.' R6: 'Secure Boot certificates... are set to expire starting in June 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: Both sources directly state older certificates expire in June 2026.

verifications.claim: The April 2026 Windows update ensures Secure Boot is active to prevent malware at startup.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Secure Boot... thwarts bootkit malware as soon as you turn on your PC... new visual clue and description to indicate the status of Secure Boot... green icon means... protected'
verifications.reasoning: Update provides status check and certificates to support Secure Boot against malware, but does not directly 'ensure' it is active; describes status indication and purpose broadly.

verifications.claim: The April 2026 Windows update confirms if a PC is fully protected via the Windows Update settings page.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R4: 'In Windows 11, go to Settings, select Privacy & security, choose Windows Security... Device security. Scroll down to the Secure Boot setting.'
verifications.reasoning: Update confirms Secure Boot status via Windows Security > Device security, not Windows Update settings page; specific path contradicts claim.

verifications.claim: Official support for Windows 10 ends October 14, 2025.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Support for Windows 10 has ended on October 14, 2025' R5: 'Windows 10 reached end of support on October 14, 2025'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple Microsoft sources directly confirm exact date.

verifications.claim: Extended Security Updates (ESU) for Windows 10 are available for purchase after October 14, 2025.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Extended Security Updates (ESU) will ensure your Windows 10 PC continues to receive important security updates until October 13, 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: Confirms ESU available post-end-of-support (Oct 14, 2025), but does not explicitly state 'for purchase'; implies paid enrollment.

verifications.claim: Forbes reported an active, dangerous fake update campaign.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Dangerous Fake Microsoft Windows Update Confirmed—Do Not Download... fake Microsoft support website... malware that is being distributed by a fake Microsoft support site'
verifications.reasoning: Forbes article (R2) directly reports on active dangerous fake Windows update campaign.

verifications.claim: ZDNET provided official confirmation of the Secure Boot protection update.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Microsoft's latest Windows update now confirms if your PC is Secure Boot-protected - how it works'
verifications.reasoning: ZDNET (R4) reports and describes the Secure Boot update from Microsoft, but is not an 'official' Microsoft source; provides confirmation via journalism.

verifications.claim: Windows 10 and Windows 11 Patch Tuesday updates became available on April 14, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'April Patch Tuesday rollout... released on April 14, 2026.' R4: 'April Patch Tuesday updates for Windows 11 and Windows 10' R8: Multiple entries 'Release date... Apr 14, 2026' for Win10/11 KBs
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Patch Tuesday updates for Win10/11 released April 14, 2026.
